events.title: Communication Protocol
events.setup: Who controls emergency communications? Webb wants corporate to manage messaging (consistent, controlled). Chen wants government emergency channel (public trust, independence).

events.title: Union Meeting Timing
events.setup: Maria Santos wants to hold emergency union meeting during work hours. This will halt processing for 2 hours but let workers voice concerns. Management says wait until after shift.

events.title: Resource Pre-Staging
events.setup: Limited generators and medical supplies must be pre-staged. Each parish wants resources in their territory. Centralizing at Heartland enables redistribution but means some parishes start with nothing.

events.title: Last Production Run
events.setup: Hurricane watch just issued. One more production cycle completes in 18 hours—worth $43M and fulfilling a contract that keeps 200 jobs secure. Storm could arrive in 48-72 hours.

events.title: Shelter Pre-Positioning
events.setup: Mayor Chen wants to open shelters now and pre-position supplies. This costs money and may be unnecessary. Waiting until warning saves money but reduces preparation time.

events.title: Information Disclosure
events.setup: Meridian has internal models showing 70% chance of direct hit—higher than public forecasts. Releasing this could cause panic. Withholding it means people make decisions on incomplete information.

events.title: Tourist Evacuation Priority
events.setup: Last commercial flights are filling. Tourists with expensive tickets get priority, but Gateway residents need those seats too. Resort owner pressures for tourist priority to "protect reputation."

events.setup: Union rep Maria Santos demands port closure 24 hours before mandatory. This protects workers but strands three supply ships with $8M in cargo and blocks the last evacuation route by sea.

events.setup: Tanaka wants to begin power rationing to build generator reserves. This means rolling brownouts for Sterling (lowest Meridian percentage) while Keystone and Summit maintain full power.

events.title: School Closure Timing
events.setup: Schools are scheduled to remain open tomorrow. Closing early lets families prepare, but many parents work at Meridian and cannot leave to pick up children. Keeping open provides childcare but risks children in transit if storm accelerates.

events.title: Executive Evacuation

T+24:00: Recovery Begins

events.title: Lessons Learned
events.setup: Final reflection session. What changes should be made? Options range from minor process tweaks to fundamental restructuring of corporate-community relationship.

events.title: Worker Compensation
events.setup: Workers lost wages during storm shutdown. Santos demands full pay for missed shifts plus hazard bonus. Corporate offers 50% with no bonus, citing losses.

events.title: Infrastructure Blame
events.setup: Dam held but barely. Investigation asks: was it maintenance deferral or act of God? Tanaka knows maintenance was deferred due to budget cuts Webb approved. Truth protects Tanaka but exposes corporate.

events.title: Production Restart Timing
events.setup: Storm passed. Clean rooms need assessment before restart. Webb wants production ASAP. Reeves says proper safety checks take 72 hours. Rushing risks contamination.

events.title: Public Narrative
events.setup: Media wants the story. Options: unified corporate/government message (controlled but may feel hollow), independent accounts (authentic but may be contradictory), or full transparency (all documents released).

events.title: Board Report
events.setup: Board demands report on storm response. Webb can present honest assessment (admits failures), spin positive (minimizes problems), or blame-shift (identifies scapegoats).
